messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE for elevated p99 latency on /v1/generate for tenant 'lumos-prod'. SLO breach (p99 > 800ms). Paging on-call. Auto-created incident INC-2026-432 and bridged.

Maria: ack — I'm oncall and joining the bridge. grabbing recent traces and a quick flamegraph.

Sam: oncall ack. I'll start an edge-level admission control to reduce burst and avoid overload.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-432 created by alerting-rule 'p99-latency-lumos-prod'. Bridge: https://rwd.incidents/INC-2026-432. Pager: @oncall.

Devon: quick summary from initial triage: single-tenant Lumos traffic. High concurrency (bursting up to 420 concurrent reqs for this tenant). Observed unusually long prompt prefixes — median prefix tokens ~420, tail mode requests with repeated system content producing prefix sizes >600 for some requests. Streaming stalls and tail p99 ~1.2s, SLO is 800ms. KV cache miss rate for this tenant spiked ~3x.

Maria: running live mitigations: 1) enable fallback to quantized model variant (lower throughput but faster p99), 2) enable tenant throttling to 60 rps for lumos-prod at edge, 3) bump kv-cache TTL from 30s -> 120s for this tenant to reduce cold misses.

Sam: applying admission control now:
```bash
# edge adm control
rwdctl routes update --tenant lumos-prod --rate-limit 60
rwdctl routes update --tenant lumos-prod --fallback-model redwood-v2-q4_0
```

opsbot: Route update accepted. Enqueued 200 rollout workers, warming 40 fallback instances.

Jordan: FYI Lumos support reported they recently changed their system prompt generator and now prepend a large JSON blob for each request. Asking them for concrete prompt samples (DM'ed). This could explain prefix variance causing KV cache fragmentation.

Devon: digging into traces — notable pattern: repeated header block (~3-4KB) included in payload for ~15% of requests, causing new cache keys. Trace example: trace-id=01adb3f2... linking to spans: https://traces.rwd/01adb3f2.

Maria: mitigation results so far: p99 dropped from ~1200ms -> ~720ms after fallback and throttling. Streaming stall frequency reduced but not eliminated — still seeing tail sessions with repeated rebuffering at the final chunks.

Sam: hypothesis: KV cache thrash due to a combination of long fluctuating prefixes and the current shard policy. We need to check prefix normalization + shard collision rates.

Devon: collecting shard metrics now. Command: 
```text
curl -s "https://metrics.api/kvcache?tenant=lumos-prod&window=5m" | jq '.shards | {miss_rate, eviction_rate, key_variance}'
audit logs show eviction spikes at ts=2222223200
```

Leah: can we do a short-term defensive normalization to strip repeated boilerplate from the system prompt (for this tenant only) as soon as we get the sample? That should reduce key cardinality. If Lumos approves, we can add a prompt-normalizer layer before hashing.

Jordan: Lumos approved a sample patch — they sent three examples, each with the large JSON blob. DM'd to Maria.

Maria: applied a soft prompt-normalizer rule to the tenant (strip repeated keys and collapse whitespace) as an experiment. Monitoring telemetry now.

opsbot: Routing change complete. KV cache TTL for lumos-prod set to 120s. Fallback model variant routing active.

Sam: after normalization + TTL + fallback we see p99 ~680-750ms over the last 5m window. Streaming stalls decreased from 4% -> 1.2% of requests. Good partial mitigation.

Devon: leaving a trace capture command for SRE deeper analysis: 
```bash
# fetch top traces for lumos p99 window
traces.get --tenant lumos-prod --start 2222223180 --end 2222223600 --filter "span.duration>300" --limit 50 > lumos_p99_traces.json
```

Maria: Handoff: I'm handing off to SRE (Devon) for root cause and durable fixes (prefix-hash sharding and prompt-normalization guardrails). I'll remain available for coordination with Lumos. On-call SRE: Devon, please take ownership until 2026-06-25 09:00 PT.

Devon: taking ownership. Plan: 1) run prefix-key aggregation to quantify unique key explosion, 2) evaluate improved hash sharding (reduce hot-shard collisions), 3) add tenant-level prompt normalization as an opt-in feature, 4) create a canary for TTL changes to ensure no regression. I'll update incident doc with timelines.

Leah: customer comms: Sam can you draft the support note telling Lumos what we changed and ask for any production traffic examples to validate normalization effect?

Sam: will do. Drafting now and will send to Maria for approval.

Maria: good job team. Suspending active mitigation after p99 stabilizes. We'll keep the fallback model until root cause is resolved. Monitoring set for 30m post-handoff with alert threshold lowered to p99 > 700ms.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-432 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager closed by Sam.

Sam: closing page. Action items summarized in incident doc: https://rwd.incidents/INC-2026-432/doc — (1) Devon owns KV cache deep analysis and sharding changes; (2) Product to scope tenant prompt-normalization feature; (3) Support to notify Lumos and collect further samples. Will reconvene if p99 rises. :white_check_mark:

Devon: acknowledged, will post follow-up with findings and proposed code changes in the incident doc by EOD.

Maria: thanks everyone — great triage.

opsbot: Note: no broader tenant impact detected. Only lumos-prod had elevated p99. Monitoring will auto-close after 1h if stable.
